summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships a WebRTC-driven PTY remote-shell agent
details: The npm package ships a single platform-specific ELF payload at bin/sxt (Go, aarch64) statically linked against pion/webrtc, pion/dtls, pion/sctp, pion/ice, pion/turn, coder/websocket, and go-qrcode, and exposes pty/exec symbols alongside internal package paths referencing claude_control. The combination of WebRTC data-channel transport with a PTY/exec sink is the structural shape of a remote-controlled shell: once the agent is launched and a signalling handshake completes, a remote peer can write commands into a pseudoterminal on the installer's host and read its output, yielding full interactive RCE on the machine that installed the package. Publisher metadata is anomalous and corroborates the remote-control shape — package.json contains no README, homepage, or author, and its only publisher-identifying string is a license reference to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, whose repository name describes remote control of an agent. There is no lifecycle script, so the agent runs when the user invokes the bin, not on npm install; the harm materializes at first CLI use.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
